hook_text: Trucks wait at a river. On the other side is a different country. What makes it different?
clip_script: Beitbridge, Limpopo. A line of trucks crosses the bridge over the Limpopo River into Zimbabwe. That river is a border, the line where one country ends and another begins. A country has its own government, laws, flag and money. Africa has fifty-four of them. Each has a capital city, where its government works. South Africa has three: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein. Some borders follow rivers, some run through lakes, and some are straight lines drawn long ago.
visual_style: Whiteboard map of southern Africa with a dashed border tracing itself along the Limpopo River and stars marking capital cities.
mood: Curious and busy, like a crowded border crossing.
pacing: Quick shots of trucks and passports, then slow tracing of borders on the map.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find three borders that follow rivers on a map of Africa.
